title: Per-impression budget charging for ad campaigns
name: Impression budget charging

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code computes and records the monetary cost of an impression? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
The same impression ID is submitted to charge() twice, for example by two ad servers that both logged the impression. What is the result of the second call?
choices: It charges the campaign a second time, because the spend update does not look at the impression.
It throws an SQLException from the primary key on charged_impressions.
It returns false: the insert with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING affects 0 rows, so the transaction is rolled back before any spend is added.
It returns true without changing anything, because the claim is treated as already successful.

questions.prompt: Two servers charge the same campaign at the same moment when exactly enough budget remains for one impression. What prevents both from succeeding?
choices: The conditional UPDATE locks the campaign_spend row, so the second transaction re-evaluates 'spent + cost <= budget' after the first commits and updates 0 rows.
The first transaction's insert into charged_impressions blocks the second.
Nothing; both succeed and the campaign slightly overspends.
The Java caller must hold a lock, since the check is done in the application.

questions.prompt: charge() returns false because the daily budget is exhausted. Which statement about that impression is correct?
choices: It is permanently marked as charged and can never be billed.
Its charged_impressions row was rolled back, so a later call with the same ID can still be charged if budget becomes available.
It is charged to the next day's spend row automatically.
It is charged partially, up to the remaining budget.
